extraction.name: AMASS (Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes)
extraction.description: AMASS is a large database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets into a common framework using the SMPL body model. It contains more than 40 hours of motion data, spanning over 300 subjects and more than 11,000 motions. The dataset is created using MoSh++, a method that converts mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.rai:dataCollection: 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets were unified using MoSh++ to convert mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet, while several others were obtained privately or recorded by the authors. Manual inspection was performed to correct or exclude problematic data (swapped/mislabeled markers). The SSM dataset was recorded using an OptiTrack mocap system with 67 markers synchronized with a 4D scanning system.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers were manually inspected and either corrected or held out (excluded).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Optical marker-based motion capture data from 15 different mocap datasets, each recorded with varying numbers of markers placed at different body locations. The SSM dataset additionally includes synchronized 4D body scans.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Inherent problems with mocap data such as swapped and mislabeled markers required manual inspection and correction or exclusion of problematic data.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Human body shape and pose data from 346 subjects captured via motion capture.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for use in human motion analysis and synthesis, providing a large-scale public resource of human shape and pose data.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Missing markers are handled using a missing-marker coefficient q during pose estimation optimization
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Manual inspection and correction of mocap data to handle swapped and mislabeled markers; problematic sequences were corrected or held out
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MoSh++ was used to map marker data into SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. This involved a two-stage fitting process: Stage I optimizes poses, shape, and latent marker positions using 12 randomly chosen frames; Stage II fits the full motion sequence. Hyperparameters were tuned via line search cross-validation on the SSM dataset.

name.evidence: we introduce AMASS, a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization.

description.evidence: Our dataset is significantly richer than previous human motion collections, having more than 40 hours of motion data, spanning over 300 subjects, more than 11000 motions, and will be publicly available to the research community.
